newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia steel shareholder says has won rights row.
newsitem.headline: Russia steel shareholder says has won rights row.

text.p: A Russian regional court has ruled in favour of a minority shareholder at Russian steelmaker Novolipetsk Metals Combine (NLMK), and this could open the door for three companies to receive seats on the board.

Renaissance Capital, which is seeking board representation, said in a statement Lipetsk Arbitration Court had ordered the steelmaker's board of directors to include nominees from fellow shareholder Bank MFK on a list of candidates to the board.

"Lawyer Larisa Ryabchenko, who represents interests of the (State Property Committee), MFK and Renaissance Capital, considers this decision has breached the armour of systematic violations of shareholders' rights at NLMK," Renaissance said.
The statement said further hearings were expected on May 14 and 21 on proceedings launched by Renaissance investment arm, the Sputnik Fund, and by U.S. investment fund Cambridge Capital Management.
MFK, which is linked to powerful Uneximbank (Oneksimbank in Russian), owns 15 percent of the Novolipetsk plant.
Cambridge, which owns 17.2 percent, and the Sputnik Fund, which owns nine percent, say management has refused to consider their candidates to its board of directors.
Senior Novolipetsk managers could not be reached for comment on Wednesday.
